clue.text: Coach constrained back causing fracas

indicators.note: back asks for the word meaning constrained to be read from its end towards its start

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
put as in hard put, forced or pressed by circumstances

explanation.surface: A sports coach, held back from the touchline, provokes a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Constrained reads as put in the sense of hard put, forced by circumstances; the coach is a vehicle, not a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is a noisy quarrel or brawl, the same as a fracas.

clue.text: End of Big Bertha's dins reverberating? Bikini followed it much later (12, two words)

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The roar of the Big Bertha howitzer in the Great War, with Bikini Atoll's bomb tests decades later.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bertha and Bikini both summon weapons, but the Bikini here is the swimsuit, which arrived long after the modest one-piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing dress was the full-cover women's swimming costume that the two-piece bikini replaced in the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Paul's excited about teaching of religion increasing

about means the mixed letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject

explanation.surface: Paul gets worked up over the growing teaching of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the British school name for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisal is a rare word for a rising up, and the definition reads as a noun: an increase.

clue.text: Bone: start of problem cutting more than one saddle up

a letter cutting a word is set inside it

a saddle is a rider's seat, and more than one makes it plural

explanation.surface: A horse rider's injury: a bone broken by a problem with saddles.
explanation.walkthrough: SEATS reversed is STAES, and P goes in after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes, or stirrup, is the small bone of the middle ear, named for its stirrup shape.

clue.text: You'll be shocked with lunch (odd bits only) — outrageous

the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The 'll of You'll is just the link to be shocked; YOU plus three letters of lunch rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Unholy is an informal intensifier for something dreadful or outrageous, as in an unholy row.

clue.text: Patches bearing plumes Private dressed early

blocks.note: Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier puts on his plumed patches before dawn parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Private looks like an adjective but is the soldier's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterylae are the tracts of a bird's skin from which feathers grow, the feathered patches.

clue.text: Handle inlaid with iron found in Scottish temple,…

clue.text: Electrical unit distorted when stripped of casing?

explanation.walkthrough: TAMPERED loses its T and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere, or amp, is the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Former lover in France, Gaston's love, dead

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's old flame, his great love, has died.

explanation.definitionFit: Friend once meant a lover or sweetheart, a sense now archaic, so a lover of former times.

clue.text: Expel some of college's tearaways

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

the first use of the jumbled word
timber is wood
twice: the jumbled word used again

explanation.surface: A piglet in a filthy pen, wallowing among bits of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The little pig is a toe, from the nursery rhyme This little piggy; the twin jumbled sty sits either side of WOO (wood cut short).

clue.text: … Half of which rang out thrillingly in part of Latin hymn (10, two words)

blocks.clueFragment: Half of which rang out thrillingly
blocks.note: surface reading: a bell or trumpet sounding out excitingly
setter's reading: the closing verses of Aquinas's eucharistic hymn, sung on their own at Benediction

explanation.surface: Continuing 6, half of a Scottish temple rings out with a thrilling sound during a Latin hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plain anchor; the opening words are a loose cryptic hint at the well-known sung section rather than a letter-by-letter build.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantum Ergo is the name given to the final two stanzas of Pange Lingua, a Latin hymn by Thomas Aquinas.

clue.text: Breath tube, the one motorists must fill?

blocks.note: plain reading: the airway from throat to lungs
surface reading: the tube a motorist blows into at a roadside breath test

explanation.surface: A roadside breath test, where the driver must fill the tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: every motorist blowing into a breathalyser fills their own windpipe first.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube that carries breath to the lungs.

clue.text: Carried like e.g. US babies in belt with soft lining

explanation.walkthrough: HIT lined with P gives HIPT, a Chambers form of hipped: American mothers famously carry babies on the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hipt means carried on the hip, as American parents are said to carry infants.

clue.text: Have deep aversion for some French oral perhaps

an oral is a spoken examination, one kind of test

explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe, to feel a deep dislike for something.

clue.text: Concealed connection run from van? (8, two words)

explanation.walkthrough: Van looks like a vehicle but is the leading part of an army; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly front is a strip of cloth covering the fastening of a garment, so the join is hidden.

blocks.note: taken as written
a lift is a boost of spirits, elation

clue.text: Name a spot that's unpleasant

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
taken as written
a sty or stye is an inflamed spot on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Pointing out a place that is grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant are ordinary synonyms for something disagreeable.

clue.text: Portraitist clothes wife alongside duke in blue fashion

blocks.note: Sir Peter Lely, court painter to Charles II
W is the abbreviation for wife
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.walkthrough: W and D sit side by side, and LELY wraps round the pair. Blue here means smutty, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means indecent, so doing something in a blue way is doing it lewdly.

taken as written

the first letter of the word

clue.text: Brain tumour maybe cut from seraglio maiden

clue.text: Emolliate dosage that's lethal in air

clue.text: Spicy Asian dish: you'll find a mixture of types near the equator
